doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Later life, Terry Gibbs and Artie Shaw
title: Eddie Daniels, and his students Ronnie Aldrich and Steve Botek
summary: He praises Eddie Daniels and explains why he taught only two people.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Was Eddie playing when you were just there, just for IAJE?
Yeah, he was playing at the Iridium.
I mean not IAJE. [laughter]
In fact, he dedicated two nights to me, you know.
That’s nice.
And Paquito came over and played.
Where was he playing?
Iridium in New York.
Oh, that’s nice.
And Ronnie Aldrich came and played.
Your disciples.

Yeah, my disciples. Well, I kind of take the credit for discovering, partially discovering, Eddie Daniels. That’s when he was with the Thad Jones—Mel Lewis band. He’s one of the best I’ve ever heard on it.
You mentioned Ron Aldrich, who was one of your very few students. You haven’t really taught many, you have chosen not to teach people.

No. I taught he and, for a short time, Steve Botek, who is a psychiatrist now and has been for several years, and a good clarinetist, he doesn’t play that much anymore. But I taught Ronnie for almost a year.
And why just those two guys? I’m sure you had a lot of people coming to you asking for lessons.
Yeah, those two guys stood out as having enough musical ability to make it worth my while [humorously].
[laughter]

Because the most frustrating thing is trying to teach somebody who doesn’t have it, so I wouldn’t do that. But Ronnie Aldrich, he’s an amazing guy, he’s written a fantastic book among other things, not really related to jazz or music. He’s one of the best the best periodontists in the country, or in the world maybe, and he goes to Italy several times to lecture on periodontal achievements. And he’s an excellent clarinet player.
And he treats all the musicians, doesn’t he, in New York?
He treats many musicians and he saved many musicians’ teeth, including mine.
